newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares rise on earnings hopes.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares rise on earnings hopes.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices closed higher on Wednesday, with investor encouraged by one listed firm which reported that its net earnings for 1996 had surged dramatically, brokers said.
The B share index gained 2.45 points or 1.68 percent to close at 148.23 on turnover of HK$95.00 million, compared with the previous session's HK$62.67 million.
The A share index rose 5.66 points or 1.62 percent to end at 355.88, with turnover expanding to 6.77 billion yuan from 4.57 billion yuan on Tuesday.
Hainan Minyuan Modern Agriculture Development Co Ltd said in its annual report on Wednesday that 1996 audited net profits were 485.29 million yuan, against 1995's 375,704 yuan.
"Market sentiment was improved by the report and it fueled buying interest in other issues likely to post good results for last year," a broker with a major Chinese brokerage said.

Trading in Minyuan on the A share market was suspended on Wednesday morning, after the report's release, and resumed in the afternoon. Minyuan closed up 0.30 yuan at 24.30 yuan on trade of 19.45 million shares.

Bulldozer manufacturer Shandong Shantui Engineering Machinery Co Ltd, which listed 88.60 million A shares and 12.50 million staff shares in Shenzhen on Wednesday, ended the session at 9.28 yuan on the heaviest volume of 77.75 million shares.
The A shares were issued on the Shenzhen bourse last month at 4.28 yuan each. The staff shares were offered at 1.20 yuan each in 1993.
Guangzhou Dongfang Hotel closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 8.24 yuan. There had been widespread talk the hotel's 1996 net earnings would be better than expected, brokers said.
All 43 Shenzhen-listed B shares traded and gained on Wednesday.
Fiyta, the biggest gainer, rose HK$0.32 or 5.61 percent to HK$6.02 on volume of 477,724 shares due to investor confidence over the Shenzhen-based watch maker's 1996 results, brokers said.
Beverage maker Shenbao, Tuesday's biggest loser, rallied HK$0.22 or 4.68 percent to HK$4.92.
China Bicycle was the most active share on volume of 1.92 million shares and climbed HK$0.13 to HK$3.98 due in part to investor confidence in its earnings outlook, brokers said.
